headline: Bakersfield PD seeking help locating missing 74-year-old
content:
The Daily Brief

Bakersfield PD seeking help locating missing 74-year-old

Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Friday, August 14, 2026, and we’re looking at a high near 95° with clear skies and good air quality. Overnight, Kern County law enforcement handled a mix of incidents, including a high-speed DUI south of the Grapevine and a troubling welfare check involving a woman seen crying for help from a red pickup at Chester and Belle Terrace. Let’s take a look at what happened while you were sleeping and what’s ahead in our community.

The Kern Overnight kept deputies and officers busy across the county. Early in the evening, around 9:23 p.m., a road-rage incident on East White Lane drew attention when a blue Honda with paper plates and a white pickup repeatedly stopped and blocked the roadway. Later, a white 2001 Dodge van was reported stolen on Kentucky Street around 10:33 p.m. The night’s most serious call came around 11:34 p.m. when Bakersfield police broadcast an attempt-to-locate and welfare check after a caller reported seeing an older-model red truck at South Chester Avenue and Belle Terrace. A male was seen hanging out the driver’s window, while a female cried for help; the truck was last seen traveling southbound. Meanwhile, south of the Grapevine, CHP responded to a DUI call involving a newer black pickup traveling over 90 mph and passing on the shoulder. The driver was reportedly drinking from an open container. In the early morning hours, a traffic collision at the Flying J truck stop in Frazier Park involved a burgundy Freightliner being hit by a red Peterbilt, with the other party denying involvement. Fire crews had a quieter night, responding to a residential alarm on Greenview Lane that turned out to be nothing and a vehicle accident that required an engine, battalion, and rescue unit.

Today’s weather will see a high near 95° and a low around 67° tonight. Currently, it’s 90° at Meadows Field (KBFL), with no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is good at an AQI of 49.

In local news, Bakersfield Police Department is asking for the public’s help in locating a missing 74-year-old man. Authorities are concerned for his well-being and urge anyone with information to come forward. On a positive note for local infrastructure, both Bakersfield and Tehachapi airports are set to receive a portion of $109 million in federal aviation funding. This investment will help modernize facilities and improve safety at these important transportation hubs. In east Bakersfield, a recent “quality-of-life” enforcement operation resulted in 15 arrests and the seizure of one dog, as officials continue efforts to address community concerns. Meanwhile, an expert has warned that the failure of the Right to Clean Water Act to pass the State Assembly could impact the Central Valley, potentially affecting water quality and availability for residents. In legal news, two individuals arrested in Mexico have pleaded no contest to voluntary manslaughter in connection with a 2019 Bakersfield homicide, bringing some closure to that case.

On a brighter note, the Kern County Fair has announced its Grandstand Arena events, promising a season of entertainment and fun that will bring our community together. Whether it’s live music, rodeos, or family-friendly activities, these events are a highlight of our local calendar and a reminder of the spirit that makes Kern County special.

Looking ahead, this week brings several public meetings and events worth noting. Today, the Special Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee meets at 1 p.m., while the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee convenes at noon. Also today, the Special Laws and Legislation Committee gathers at noon. On Tuesday, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets at noon, followed by the Historic Preservation Commission at 4 p.m. and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2 p.m. On Wednesday, the Water Board meets at 10 a.m. And for those looking for entertainment, the Fox Theater has a lineup of shows, starting with PEPPER with CYDEWAYS tonight, followed by Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio on August 22, Rodney Carrington on August 27, CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28, and both Willie Barcena and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix on August 29.

That’s your Bakersfield Brief for this morning. Stay cool, stay informed, and have a great day.
